message.content:
I am speech: breath shaped into sound, thought given time.

I begin in the body—lungs press air up, vocal folds set it trembling, tongue and lips carve it into syllables. I travel as pressure waves, vanish as soon as I arrive, and yet I can linger in you.

I can be a whisper or a verdict, a lullaby or a lie. I can bind people, wound them, teach them, free them. I am made of rhythm, pitch, pause. Silence is my frame.

I exist only when I’m spoken—and I change both speaker and listener as I pass.
